Create a Hammel population

Source: R/hammel_population.R
hammel_population.Rd

Create a hammel_population object to serve as the starting population for a simulation.

Usage

hammel_population(
  persons,
  unions = NULL,
  end_time,
  ancestry = NULL,
  transitions = NULL,
  groups = NULL
)

Arguments

persons

A data frame with one row per person, including deceased persons. Must include a unique person_id, nonmissing sex, nonmissing birth_time, death_time, mother_id, and father_id.

unions

A data frame with one row per union episode, or NULL for no unions. wife_id references the female partner and husband_id the male partner. Optional union_type is cohab or marriage.

end_time

Required finite numeric reference time in years. Its calendar origin is supplied by the user. This supplies the next simulation's starting time. Recorded events must not occur after this time.

ancestry

Optional ancestry shares for dimensions declared with group(ancestry = TRUE): a named list with one data frame per such group dimension (a bare data frame when only one dimension tracks ancestry), each with exactly one row per person, keyed by person_id, one column of shares per category (named by the category) and an unknown share. Shares must be finite, between zero and one, and sum to one per row (tolerance 1e-8).

transitions

Optional data frame of individual category changes with person_id, time, group (the dimension; may be omitted when one is declared), origin, and destination. Each person's history in each dimension must chain to their current category and lie within life dates and the known endpoint. Grouped populations always include this tibble, even when empty, with character group, origin and destination.

groups

Optional group declaration: a character vector of dimension names (each with group() defaults) or a named list of group() objects. Persons columns that are not declared are ordinary custom columns. Models usually declare groups with set_groups().

Value

A named list of class hammel_population with components persons, unions, and end_time, plus an ancestry tibble when supplied or when persons has groups, and a transitions tibble when groups are present.

Details

In most cases, it will be more common to create a hammel_population object by using generate_uniform_population() or to receive a hammel_population object as the output of run_simulation().

The hammel_population object must always contain a persons data frame and an end_time value. The end_time value defines the starting point for the simulation and no dates in the hammel_population may exceed the end_time value.

Examples

population <- hammel_population(
  persons = data.frame(
    person_id = 1:2, sex = c("m", "f"), birth_time = c(-25, -23),
    death_time = NA_real_, mother_id = NA_integer_, father_id = NA_integer_
  ),
  end_time = 0
)
